Yesterday, my partner and I went to a local tattoo shop for their Friday the 13th special. Deal is for $13 with a tip you get a 13th themed tattoo from some fresh flash! The shop is located on a pedestrian shopping thoroughfare very popular in my city and there is a festival season going on, so we have lots of [drunk] people out.  

As we were leaving, a fresh-faced tall, slender young lady was speaking to an artist, grown man barking little quips and bro-shouting about the shop. (Shop culture. I get it. But still.) If you think I'm framing this against him, he had some nice-ass work on him and cool taste in music.  

"You got your ID with you?" he asks. She shakes her head, looking a little flustered. 

"How about a passport, hmm? Student ID?" he probes in the most patronizing voice I have ever had the displeasure of hearing. "Hmmm, okayyyyee. Well you could be 18 but how do I know that? How do you just walk around like that? Hope they identify you? What happens when you get on the bus?" 

That last one got me. Then we were out of the shop. I actually became nauseous.  

Look, I get it, Tattoo Guy. I've worked at places you have to ID people. I get that it's the customer's burden to prove their age. But to speak to someone like that is just not a good look. He could have taken the high road and said, "Sorry, you must prove your age," or even shorter, "No ID, no ink." But no. He chose to be completely fucking rude. I take his side 100%, no doubt. If she was 17 and the Tattoo SWAT Team got wind of the pedo-inking, they'd go down. Hard. The worst part is that this probably happens daily and he goes out of his way to be mean, when you can just be more efficient/happier by being nicer and sticking to the point. Unfortunately, if you're in the service industry, you have to deal with...people!! 

Being spoken to like that in public is humiliating and degrading, no matter what. (It's happened to me before, and it was because they got my order wrong and refused to inform me of products on sale. All somehow my fault.) You might think it's exhibiting policies, but you're really just a fucking asshole. I wish I could have told him he could have shoved two burgers in his fart sucker in the time he spouted mean shit to the nice young lady, who was already clearly embarrassed before he starting reaming into her.

TL;DR - Asshole tattoo dude talks condescendingly as hell to someone, yet understandably so. Still remains major asshole.
